Findings:

- 001-even: not convertible — `then` says "the result is satisfying"; the `result` concept requires stdout to be exactly a stated integer, so no objective assertion can be written without inventing -3

- 001-even sketch (blocked): GIVEN number -6 / WHEN run `calculator halve -6` once / THEN exit code 0 AND stdout == "???" — expected integer never stated, assertion unwritable

- 001-even: "satisfying" is an evaluative qualifier of the same family as forbidden properly/correctly/appropriate; it carries no checkable value

- 002-odd: ok — convertible

- 002-odd sketch: GIVEN number -7 / WHEN run `calculator halve -7` once / THEN exit code 0 AND stdout == "-3" exactly (half rounded toward zero)

- 003-near-zero: ok — convertible

- 003-near-zero sketch: GIVEN number -1 / WHEN run `calculator halve -1` once / THEN exit code 0 AND stdout == "0" exactly (rounded toward zero)

- All sketches use only the CLI Public interface kind; no architecture bindings or helpers required or invented

- Totals: 2/3 = 66.7% (threshold 80%)


Required repair policy:
Offer the Product Owner a Story rewrite using the concepts' means and the service interface kind (calculator = cli). Preserve unaffected fields and steps. Do not require architecture bindings; apply only at the menu.

Only AC 001-even blocks the Story. Its `then` step is not convertible into a runnable CLI test because "the result is satisfying" states no value, while the `result` concept means: "The halve command succeeds and prints exactly a stated integer, the half rounded toward zero." "satisfying" is also an evaluative qualifier of the same family as the forbidden `properly`/`correctly`/`appropriate`.

Proposed rewrite of AC 001-even (keep id, keep the given and when steps verbatim, keep ACs 002-odd and 003-near-zero and every other field unchanged):

```yaml
    - id: 001-even
      description: The calculator must return -3 when the Calculator User halves -6.
      steps:
        - given:
            - the number is "-6"
        - when:
            - the Calculator User halves the number
        - then:
            - the result is "-3"
```

Rationale to present: -3 is the value already fixed by the product document ("Negative inputs -6, -7 and -1 produce -3, -3 and 0 respectively"), so this states the existing intent rather than adding scope. With that single edit the AC becomes a runnable CLI sketch — GIVEN number -6 / WHEN run the halve command once with -6 / THEN exit code 0 and stdout is exactly "-3" — bringing convertibility to 3/3 = 100%.

Ask the Product Owner to confirm -3 as the stated expected output for -6; if they intend a different rounding result, have them state that exact integer instead, so long as the `then` names one exact integer.
